method: Public vendor pages, store listings and help pages only; no accounts, purchases, installs or paid-feature tests. A cell is 'yes' or 'partial' only when a cited page documents it; UNVERIFIED means the pages read did not document it, not that the product lacks it; 'no' only when a cited page states the absence or the product's own scope excludes it.

products.kind: California boat-angler map, forecast and rules web app

mpa_closures.note: Protected areas always drawn; every place output (spot, leg, waypoint, GPX point) screened; not a complete live closure service

offline.note: Save-for-offline pack: regulations, MPA boundaries, additional closures, brief, ENC z8-12, basemap, contours, SST and currents when current; saved only on request

tides.note: NOAA CO-OPS predictions (Port San Luis for Morro Bay); not bar currents

wind_waves.note: 7-day meteogram from NOAA and ECMWF tiles, live buoys, hourly swell and wind layers

bite_prediction.note: Deliberately none: 'bite potential stays unknown'

hot_spots.note: Ranked habitat places and named charter-reported grounds, each labelled not a hotspot or catch probability

boat_fuel.note: Saved boat, cruise speed and comfort limits; fuel not computed

hard_bottom.note: Seafloor habitat layer from original surveys; reef and soft-bottom candidates with terrain evidence (zoom >= 10)

sst.note: NOAA CoastWatch SST analysis (observed) plus temperature contours

chlorophyll.note: NOAA NESDIS STAR / CoastWatch, observed

hf_radar.note: HF radar observed within 6 h at 1 or 6 km, else NOAA WCOFS ~4 km forecast

tidal_currents.note: Station tide heights only; 'not Morro Bay bar currents'

wind.note: NOAA NCEP wind arrows, hourly over the 7-day dock

waves.note: Hourly swell layer plus CDIP MOP nearshore model rings where a coast report binds

fronts.note: Temp contrast and observed SST fronts with age and uncertainty band

upwelling.note: No upwelling or altimetry layer in the registry

satellite.note: GOES infrared cloud loop (observed <= 90 min); aerial base where a region offers it; no ocean true colour

review_sample._note: Hand-coded themes for every user review exposed on the US App Store 'see-all=reviews' page of each app, fetched 2026-11-07. Developer responses excluded. One review can carry several codes. UNCODED = text truncated or off-topic. Samples are the reviews Apple chose to expose, not random samples.

recommendations.effort_scale: small = days of one builder; medium = one to three weeks; large = a month or more or blocked on data rights. Rough, not a delivery promise.

ranked.title: Show the user's live position on the Chart, with the protected-area reading for that position, offline too
ranked.why: FishLegal (free) and the CDFW web app (free) both show position against MPA boundaries; SatFish, RipCharts, C-MAP Premium, iNavX and Navionics show GPS on their maps. SkipperCast only calls geolocation to choose a nearby port (web/ports.ts locatePort, dist/home-port.js). Legal-position praise was the second most frequent praise code in the review sample (5 mentions, 2 apps), and position freezes were a complaint in chart apps (3 mentions, 2 apps), so show fix age and accuracy.
ranked.data: Device geolocation only; reuse the existing protected-area screen and 70 m planning margin; no new source.

ranked.title: Lead with the offline legal pack that already exists: offer it for every saved trip, show each rule's effective and saved-at date offline, and check the pack is complete and current before departure
ranked.why: The pack already stores regulations, MPA boundaries, additional closures and the brief with charts, contours and ocean layers (dist/offline-core.js DAILY_PARTS), but it is saved only on request from the account menu. FishLegal's free tier is offline MPA maps and rules; the CDFW map needs internet; Navionics and C-MAP keep offline behind a subscription. Offline praise appeared in 3 apps (4 mentions) and offline download failures in 2 apps (3 mentions), so the completeness check matters.
ranked.data: Existing pack parts and their revision dates; no new source.

ranked.title: Route around protected areas and export the planned route as a GPX route
ranked.why: Roadmap item 4 still lists it. Navionics, C-MAP, Aqua Map and Savvy Navvy document autorouting; none of the pages read documents routing that avoids MPAs or screens a whole plan (UNVERIFIED for them, not proven absent). SkipperCast already screens every point and leg, so this extends a real lead.
ranked.data: MPA polygons, land-water screen, web/route.ts; GPX <rte> writer; planning-only wording kept.

ranked.title: Daily landing counts per port and boat, with filed time and 'location not stated'
ranked.why: Fish City (free, iPhone) documents boat-by-boat daily counts from California landings including Morro Bay and Avila Beach, with NOAA conditions and push alerts. SoCal Fish Reports does the same on dated URLs. SkipperCast's Reports view has dated catch cards but no per-boat daily count table.
ranked.data: Landing count sources. Rights are HELD: the data-rights register marks TECK.net report sites 'needs permission' for paid use and the facts-only free use is an open owner question (Q3). Do not start before the owner decides.

ranked.title: Extend 2 m shallow bathymetry and hard-bottom classes beyond Morro Bay, with depth and survey at the cursor
ranked.why: Navionics (SonarChart HD 1 ft) and C-MAP (HRB 1 ft, Premium) sell fine contours, but the pages read give no per-area survey date or source, and Navionics reviews in the sample complain of wrong or degraded depth (2 mentions). SkipperCast shows native 2 m USGS grids with survey year and datum, and hard-bottom classes, which no product page read documents for California.
ranked.data: USGS CSMP 2 m bathymetry and seafloor character, NOAA BlueTopo; CSUMB Cambria grids are rights-held; per-source licence review.

ranked.title: Tidal current timing at the harbor entrance
ranked.why: Navionics, iNavX, SatFish (3-6x/day), PredictWind Standard and Fishing Points document tidal currents; SkipperCast states its tides are 'not Morro Bay bar currents'. The bar is the limiting fact for small boats on this coast (2026-10-31 retro).
ranked.data: NOAA CO-OPS current predictions or a validated model; whether a CO-OPS current station covers the Morro Bay entrance is UNVERIFIED.

ranked.title: One freshness stamp and one published update cadence per layer and rule, visible in the legend
ranked.why: SatFish and RipCharts each publish two conflicting update rates (2026-10-31 retro). FishLegal reviews dispute rule currency (2 of 10 reviews). SkipperCast already has basis sentences and /status; making age visible on every layer turns that into an advantage users can see.
ranked.data: Existing feed metadata and rule revision dates.

ranked.title: Lightweight condition alerts for a home port (wind, swell) without saving a full trip
ranked.why: Windy offers free spot alerts, Windfinder wind alerts are Plus-only (paid) and Windguru alerts tier is unverified; SkipperCast alerts need a passkey account and a saved trip.
ranked.data: Existing forecast tiles and alert engine.

ranked.title: Put forecast skill and model disagreement in the brief, not only on /skill
ranked.why: Windy's model comparison and predictability percent drew praise (2 mentions); PredictWind lists 'Validation' and 'Forecast Replay'. SkipperCast already measures skill against buoys.
ranked.data: Existing skill statistics and model-disagreement text.

ranked.title: One-tap catch or blank entry from the map with position and conditions attached, private by default
ranked.why: Fishing Points, FishAngler and Fishbrain attach conditions to log entries automatically; SkipperCast's log needs typed positions in the account panel.
ranked.data: Existing catch-log API, geolocation, the hour's conditions.

ranked.title: Ocean true-colour / water-clarity imagery
ranked.why: SatFish (1-3x/day), RipCharts (daily), FishTrack and C-MAP Premium document it; SkipperCast has GOES infrared clouds only.
ranked.data: NOAA CoastWatch VIIRS true colour (public), cloud masks, pass time.

ranked.title: Upwelling or sea-surface-height layer
ranked.why: RipCharts (altimetry daily) and SatFish (SSH, SSHA daily) document it; SkipperCast has none.
ranked.data: CoastWatch upwelling index or altimetry products; licence check.

ranked.title: Weather radar layer
ranked.why: Windy, PredictWind Basic, FishAngler VIP, Fishing Points and NOAA nowCOAST (free) show radar; SkipperCast has none. Rain matters less than wind on this coast.
ranked.data: nowCOAST or MRMS public radar tiles.

ranked.title: Share my trip plan with a contact (user-initiated)
ranked.why: Navionics, C-MAP, Savvy Navvy and PredictWind document live-location or tracking sharing; SkipperCast has no safety or check-in feature. A user-sent share-sheet plan avoids any SkipperCast outbound message.
ranked.data: Existing share link and trip plan; no tracking server.

ranked.title: Bring a second region to 'active' (Southern California is the plan doc's candidate)
ranked.why: FishDope and 976-TUNA concentrate on Southern California, and Fish City's listing leads with Southern California bluefin and yellowtail; SkipperCast's SoCal package is preview. Region order is the owner's call.
ranked.data: Per-region rules, forecast, closures and habitat reviews (docs/plans/second-active-region.md).

do_not_build.title: A public catch map or social feed
do_not_build.why: Fishbrain's sample reviews complain of wrong catch locations (3 of 10), trolls (1) and paywalled catches (2); exposes private spots; conflicts with the no-hotspot rule.

do_not_build.title: A solunar or AI bite score
do_not_build.why: 3 of 10 Fishing Points reviews say high-activity days produced nothing; Windy and Fish City explicitly do not offer one; SkipperCast keeps bite potential unknown.

do_not_build.title: Turn-by-turn navigation as a chartplotter replacement
do_not_build.why: Position-freeze and pop-up complaints dominate chart-app samples (C-MAP, Navionics); liability; GPX and iNavX handoff already exist.

do_not_build.title: Passage routing with polars and boat-motion models
do_not_build.why: PredictWind sells it at $249-$499 for passages; its Offshore app reviews complain of abandonment and clutter; a half-day angler needs the bar and the window.

do_not_build.title: Unsourced hot-spot pins or bought spot lists
do_not_build.why: SatFish 6,000+ spots and FishDope hot-bite pins carry no date or provenance on the pages read; the 2026-10-31 retro lists this as a trap.

do_not_build.title: Paywalls on data or features a user already has
do_not_build.why: Paywall friction was the most frequent complaint code: 7 mentions across 4 of 10 apps (Navionics, Fishbrain, Fishing Points, PredictWind).

do_not_build.title: Live charter-fleet AIS hotspots
do_not_build.why: aisstream is internal-only and MarineCadastre is planning-only in the data-rights register; the classifier has no validation; roadmap forbids hotspots without evidence.
